lymph node dissection is safe and can be performed with minimal risk of complications in patients with borderline ovarian tumor.
The incidence of nodal metastasis in borderline ovarian tumors is low (2.3%).

(a) The number of lymph node dissections is associated with the number of lymph nodes removed and with the number of positive lymph nodes, (b) The number of positive lymph node is associated with survival, and (c) The number of removed lymph nodes is associated with survival.

the development of a new method for the analysis of lymph nodes in patients treated for borderline ovarian tumors.
the study of the lymph node status of patients with borderline ovarian tumors.
the development and evaluation of a new method for the detection of ovarian cancer.

the lymph node metastatic rate for stage IA borderline ovarian tumors ranges between 0% and 4%.

lymphadenectomy should be considered in borderline ovarian tumors, but not in low-grade ovarian tumors, because of the low incidence of nodal involvement and the absence of prognostic value in the presence of negative nodes.
the presence of lymphadenopathy in patients with ovarian cancer is not a prognostic factor for survival.

we found that the lymph node metastasis in the patients with borderline ovarian tumors was rare and the prognosis was good.
lymph nodes should be removed in the case of a borderline ovarian tumor.
the lymph node status is an important prognostic indicator for patients with ovarian carcinoma.

the lymphatic system is a major regulator of the immune response in the gut, and that the gut lymphatic system is the primary route of immune cell trafficking to the liver, spleen and bone marrow.
